data.title: XML Sitemap
data.tagline: List important canonical URLs in a machine-readable XML file for crawler discovery
data.learningOutcome: You can decide which reachable canonical URLs belong in sitemap.xml and distinguish discovery, crawling, indexing, and site information architecture.
data.description: When a new article has few internal links, listing its full address in sitemap.xml can help crawlers discover and request it. It is a machine-readable URL list, not visitor-facing site navigation, and it does not guarantee indexing or ranking.

learning.assumes: You know that a web page opens through a URL and have heard that search systems crawl and index pages.
learning.outcome: You can decide which reachable canonical URLs belong in sitemap.xml and distinguish discovery, crawling, indexing, and site information architecture.

explanation.title: List the addresses you want systems to discover
explanation.text: A sitemap organizes full URLs in XML for important pages you want crawlers to discover. Each address should exist, be reachable, and match the page's chosen canonical address.

explanation.title: Discovery is followed by requests and decisions
explanation.text: After reading the list, a crawler still requests each page, checks access, and decides what to process. A sitemap improves discovery; it does not provide content or decide indexing and ranking.

data.boundary: An XML sitemap is a machine file for crawlers. An information-architecture sitemap or site navigation is a visible structure for people. It is not access control: listing a URL grants no permission, and omitting one does not block access.

lessonPractice.title: An entry in sitemap.xml points to an article URL that returns 404. What should you do?

options.label: Fix the article URL or remove it from the sitemap, then verify every listed URL is reachable
options.feedback: Correct. A sitemap should help crawlers find important reachable URLs; listing a broken address cannot create the missing page.

options.label: Keep it because a crawler will create or index the article after seeing the URL
options.feedback: A sitemap is a discovery hint, not a resource creator or an indexing guarantee. A 404 entry instead gives crawling an error signal.

options.label: Replace it with a visitor-facing article directory and write out the full navigation hierarchy
options.feedback: A visible directory is information architecture or site navigation, not a replacement for an XML sitemap. The broken machine URL still needs handling.

data.agentPrompt: Generate sitemap.xml with only important pages that you want crawlers to discover, using full canonical URLs that are reachable. Validate the XML and request every listed address; report which URLs succeed and which need fixing. Do not describe a sitemap as an indexing or ranking guarantee.
